results.description:
How a Village Self-Defence Group Turned Into Nigeria’s New Cross-Border Terror Bridge

In 2017, border villages in Sokoto invited an armed herding militia, Lakurawa to shield them from bandits.

By 2026, that former vigilante force had evolved into one of Nigeria’s fastest-spreading terror threats:
• Taxed Kebbi and Sokoto communities ₦50m ($36,000) in March 2026 just to let clerics preach Ramadan tafsir
• Killed 162 civilians in Woro and Nuku, Kwara State after villages rejected its rule
• Built an active corridor linking Sahelian jihadists (ISGS/JNIM) toward northern Benin and central Nigeria

History’s hardest internal security lesson repeats: when the state leaves a vacuum, outsourced community defence rarely stays defensive for long.

results.title: BREAKING UPDATE Bandits have imposed heavy levies on more than 10 communities in Bungudu Local Government Area of Zamfara State.
results.description:
BREAKING UPDATE
Bandits have imposed heavy levies on more than 10 communities in Bungudu Local Government Area of Zamfara State.
Residents were given one week to pay. Failure to do so will increase the amount, and some communities have been warned of possible attacks.
Affected communities include Kway Sukune, Gangmahanu, Maji, Tongangkune, Gandaya, Kanya, Gidang Kaima, Gidang Makere, Nambasa, Bini, Buwaye, Matere, Matsari, Makwayo, Bozaya, Sabu Watunga, Tudung Doka Miramai, Damake, Dandinding, Gidan Saru, Haidang Koro, Mashima, Hodomabika, Tunga Haki and Gidan Angu.
Amounts range from ₦10 million to ₦20 million per community.
Locals are appealing to the Federal Government and security agencies for urgent intervention.

Watch the full clips here: https://t.co/MaWh9SM3hc
